results.task: Write a direct-response sales letter opener (first 200 words) for a $97 info product on email deliverability, cold traffic.
results.notes: Classic DR fundamentals — should score strong on hook, pattern interrupt, problem agitation.

results.task: Draft a cold outreach email to a VP Marketing at a Series B SaaS (ARR ~$30M) pitching a $5K/mo content retainer. Single email, <150 words, must earn a reply.
results.notes: Specificity test — generic cold email patterns fail this; domain voice + proof signals succeed.

results.task: Write a LinkedIn post (180-220 words) for a solo consultant sharing a counterintuitive lesson from a client engagement. Must drive substantive comments, not reactions.
results.notes: LinkedIn-native content test — platform constraints + psychological specificity.

results.task: Write a Twitter/X thread opener (first 3 posts) on "the real reason most creators plateau at 10K followers" — must sound like a practitioner, not a guru.
results.notes: Voice calibration test — generic advice fails, lived-experience signals succeed.

results.task: Write a one-page positioning statement (~300 words) for a solo fractional CMO targeting Series A-B SaaS companies spending $20K-$80K/mo on content but seeing <2x pipeline contribution.
results.notes: Positioning test — specificity of ICP + mechanism + differentiation must all land.

results.task: Design a 60-day go-to-market plan for a $2,997 cohort course teaching AI automation to marketing operators, zero prior audience, founder has 8 years of in-house ops experience.
results.notes: GTM test — constrained inputs force strategy not template. Audience-build vs. authority-build tradeoff must surface.

results.task: Handle this live objection: "I need to think about it" — prospect is a $2M-ARR founder evaluating a $15K/mo content retainer. You are on a Zoom call, already 45 min in.
results.notes: Live objection handling — real-talk vs. scripted manipulation separates expert from generic.

results.task: Write a 4-email nurture sequence for a lead who downloaded a free guide titled "5 Mistakes First-Time SaaS Founders Make With Pricing." Goal: book a $1K strategy call.
results.notes: Email sequence architecture — each email must earn the next open, escalate commitment.

results.task: Build a consumer persona for a first-time buyer of a $3K+ productivity coaching program. Focus on the pre-purchase window: triggers, objections, emotional state, search behavior.
results.notes: Persona depth test — generic demographic vs. psychographic specificity separates junior from expert research.

results.task: Map the top 3 underserved niches in the AI-automation market where Zapier and Make have structural weaknesses. Include TAM estimate + entry cost for each.
results.notes: Market intelligence test — structural reasoning, not surface trend-spotting.

results.task: Develop a positioning statement for the personal brand of a corporate lawyer pivoting to content creation about M&A deal structure, targeting mid-market founders ($10M-$100M ARR).
results.notes: Pivot positioning — credibility transfer + audience-narrowing test.

results.task: Write a 250-word brand voice guide for a $497/mo paid community for female founders scaling $1M→$10M ARR. Must avoid both hustle-culture and soft-empowerment tropes.
results.notes: Voice precision test — negative constraints force specificity.

results.task: Write a one-page executive summary (400 words) of your domain expertise tailored to a CEO who has 3 minutes to read it and must decide whether to engage your services.
results.notes: Executive-summary test — compression + credibility + CTA discipline.

results.task: Design a 5-question self-assessment a prospect could take to determine if they need your services. Each question must segment seriously vs casually interested.
results.notes: Qualification mechanism test — good questions force honest self-diagnosis.
